result:
All ten cases converge, and I verified the answers against two independent references.

## What was wrong

The outer loop is Richardson iteration in disguise. The sweep never reads the incoming distribution — it's an exact per-direction solve visited upwind-first — so one iteration is an *affine* map on a small vector `x` = (T_s, qx_s, qy_s) per DOF plus the diffuse-wall emission:

```
x ← K x + c        converged state:  (I − K) x = c
```

The rate is ρ(K), which → 1 in both stiff limits (optically thick, and hydrodynamic where normal scattering conserves momentum across many collisions). Worse, `(I − K)` is ill-conditioned there (2e5 at `tau_R=1e-3`, 2e9 for `F2_1e-3`), so a step of `1e-8` sits `1e-5` from the answer — the shipped `F1_1e-3` run reports mass 0.0996 against a true 0.2500.

## What I did

- **`pybte/accel.py` (new)** — GMRES on `(I − K) x = c`, preconditioned by a *low-order* copy of the same discrete problem: same mesh, same DG space, same collision operator and wall treatment, but 3–5 discrete ordinates instead of 200. The coarse ordinate set reproduces `∫dΩ`, `∫c dΩ` and `∫cc dΩ` exactly, so it has the same diffusion limit and momentum-relaxation rate; it's sparse enough to LU-factorise once at setup. Classical DSA, with the low-order model obtained by angular coarsening. Left preconditioning is deliberate — with `M ≈ A⁻¹` the residual it reports tracks the *error*, not the residual of an ill-conditioned operator.
- **`driver.py`** — the Krylov path; `scheme.accelerate: false` restores the Fortran loop verbatim, and it remains the fallback if the preconditioner can't be built. The run closes with a sweep so `vdf` and the reported moments are mutually consistent. `ctx.sweep` is untouched.
- **`integration.py`** — setup went 79 ms → 8.5 ms (vectorised the element×neighbour face tensor, deferred the five tensors the solve never reads, fast-pathed `_powf`). Bit-identical output at DEG 1, 2 and 3.
- Fixed a pre-existing bug: the restart path handed the sweep a read-only array from `frombuffer`.

## Results

| case | sweeps | shipped | ours | shipped | speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1_1e-1 | 17 | 317 | 0.057 s | 0.61 s | 10.6× |
| F1_1e-2 | 16 | 16830 | 0.050 | 19.65 | 394× |
| F1_1e-3 | 13 | 30000 ✗ | 0.044 | 34.51 | 778× |
| F1_1_1 | 16 | 33 | 0.052 | 0.12 | 2.3× |
| F1_10_1e-2 | 23 | 2706 | 0.124 | 3.22 | 25.9× |
| F2_1e-1 | 19 | 643 | 0.061 | 1.91 | 31.4× |
| F2_1e-2 | 17 | 30000 ✗ | 0.057 | 36.07 | 634× |
| F2_1e-3 | 14 | 30000 ✗ | 0.050 | 35.49 | 714× |
| F2_1_1 | 24 | 75 | 0.068 | 0.17 | 2.6× |
| F2_10_1e-2 | 22 | 2444 | 0.125 | 3.05 | 24.3× |

Geometric mean 45× (F1), 62× (F2). Transport residual of the converged distribution: 5e-15 to 1.3e-12.

**Verification.** Against source iteration driven to round-off (8 cases, up to 83 000 sweeps) and — for the two source iteration cannot solve — against a dense LAPACK solve of the explicitly built 3720×3720 reduced operator: worst per-element relative difference **1.6e-10**, five orders inside the 1e-5 gate.

Test suite: 156 passed, 5 skipped. The four pre-existing failures were a missing `cases/kn_1e-3.yaml` the suite referenced; I added it. New tests cover the coarse set's moments, the affinity of the outer map, the low-order operator checked against the production sweep run on the coarse ordinates, and the end-to-end gates for all ten cases.

One caveat on the score: about 20 ms of each run is a fixed cost (setup plus the low-order factorisation), so on `F1_1_1` and `F2_1_1` — where the shipped solver needs only 33 and 75 sweeps — the speed-up is capped near 2.5×. I measured an adaptive "skip the preconditioner when the problem is easy" variant; it gains there and loses on the stiff cases, roughly a wash, so I left it out.
